explanation_en: This absolute participle construction ('passado' + time period) is a very common and elegant way to indicate the passage of time in Portuguese, equivalent to 'after some years' or 'a few years later'. Note that while prescriptive grammar sometimes demands agreement ('passados alguns anos'), in spoken Brazilian Portuguese it is very common to hear it left in the singular masculine form 'passado'. It is a great narrative transition device.

examples.en_text: After a few years living abroad, I decided to return to my hometown.
examples.target_text: Passados alguns anos a viver no estrangeiro, decidi voltar para a minha cidade natal.

examples.en_text: He opened a small business and, after a few years, he was already very successful.
examples.target_text: Ele abriu um pequeno negócio e, passados alguns anos, já tinha muito sucesso.

examples.en_text: We lost touch, but after a few years, we saw each other again downtown.
examples.target_text: Nós perdemos o contacto, mas, passados alguns anos, voltámos a ver-nos no centro da cidade.

examples.en_text: In the beginning it was difficult, but after a few years of practice, he already played the piano very well.
examples.target_text: No início era difícil, mas passados alguns anos de prática, ele já tocava piano muito bem.

examples.en_text: I went back to that beach and, after a few years, the landscape was completely different.
examples.target_text: Voltei àquela praia e, passados alguns anos, a paisagem estava completamente diferente.

examples.en_text: She changed her habits and, after a few years, she felt much healthier.
examples.target_text: Ela mudou os seus hábitos e, passados alguns anos, sentia-se muito mais saudável.

explanation_en: This concessive conjunction is used to express 'even though' or 'no matter how much.' It is a classic B2/C1 grammar point because it almost always triggers the subjunctive mood (e.g., 'tenha declarado'). It is highly useful in both formal writing and everyday debates to acknowledge a counter-argument.

examples.en_text: No matter how much I try, I can't understand the rules of this game.
examples.target_text: Por mais que eu tente, não consigo entender as regras deste jogo.

examples.en_text: As much as she likes chocolate, she is trying to eat fewer sweets.
examples.target_text: Por mais que ela goste de chocolate, está tentando comer menos doces.

examples.en_text: No matter how much you run, you are still going to be late for work.
examples.target_text: Por mais que você corra, ainda vai chegar atrasado ao trabalho.

examples.en_text: No matter how much we study, tomorrow's exam is going to be difficult.
examples.target_text: Por mais que nós estudemos, a prova de amanhã vai ser difícil.

examples.en_text: As much as they try to help, he prefers to do everything by himself.
examples.target_text: Por mais que eles tentem ajudar, ele prefere fazer tudo sozinho.

examples.en_text: As much as I wanted to go to the party, I had to stay home studying.
examples.target_text: Por mais que eu quisesse ir à festa, tive que ficar em casa estudando.

explanation_en: This is a standard idiomatic collocation meaning 'to take seriously.' While the individual words are simple, using 'levar' (to carry/lead) instead of 'tomar' or 'fazer' is a key idiomatic pattern in Portuguese. It is used in all registers, from casual conversations to political analyses.

examples.en_text: He never takes my opinions seriously.
examples.target_text: Ele nunca leva as minhas opiniões a sério.

examples.en_text: You have to take this matter seriously, it's very important.
examples.target_text: Tens de levar este assunto a sério, é muito importante.

examples.en_text: At first, nobody took him seriously, but now he is a famous painter.
examples.target_text: No início, ninguém o levou a sério, mas agora ele é um pintor famoso.

examples.en_text: If you don't take the warning seriously, you are going to have problems.
examples.target_text: Se não levares o aviso a sério, vais ter problemas.

examples.en_text: We take the safety of our workers very seriously.
examples.target_text: Nós levamos muito a sério a segurança dos nossos trabalhadores.

examples.en_text: Don't take what he said seriously, he was only joking.
examples.target_text: Não leves a sério o que ele disse, ele estava apenas a brincar.

explanation_en: Literally translating to 'to jump to the eyes,' this idiom means to be extremely obvious, striking, or prominent. It is a highly natural way to describe something that immediately grabs attention or stands out in a comparison. It is frequently used in analytical and journalistic contexts.

examples.en_text: The difference in quality between the two products is obvious.
examples.target_text: A diferença de qualidade entre os dois produtos salta aos olhos.

examples.en_text: When I read the report, the typos immediately stood out.
examples.target_text: Quando li o relatório, os erros de digitação saltaram logo aos olhos.

examples.en_text: It is glaringly obvious that she is not happy with her new job.
examples.target_text: Salta aos olhos que ela não está feliz com o novo emprego.

examples.en_text: In that old painting, the use of warm colors stands out.
examples.target_text: Naquela pintura antiga, o uso de cores quentes salta aos olhos.

examples.en_text: The lack of organization of the event is obvious to anyone.
examples.target_text: A falta de organização do evento salta aos olhos de qualquer pessoa.

examples.en_text: In his resume, the international experiences really stand out.
examples.target_text: No currículo dele, as experiências internacionais saltam aos olhos.

explanation_en: This past participle construction functions as an adjective meaning 'committed,' 'dedicated,' or 'striving hard' to do something. It is always followed by the preposition 'em' and an infinitive verb or noun. It is a B2/C1 level vocabulary choice that sounds much more native and professional than simply using 'querer' or 'tentar.'

examples.en_text: João is very committed to getting that promotion at work.
examples.target_text: O João está muito empenhado em conseguir aquela promoção no trabalho.

examples.en_text: She is dedicated to learning to speak Portuguese fluently this year.
examples.target_text: Ela está empenhada em aprender a falar português fluentemente este ano.

examples.en_text: The neighborhood residents are committed to keeping the park clean.
examples.target_text: Os moradores do bairro estão empenhados em manter o parque limpo.

examples.en_text: My brother is committed to improving his diet and exercising more.
examples.target_text: O meu irmão está empenhado em melhorar a sua alimentação e fazer mais exercício.

examples.en_text: They are very dedicated to finishing the project before the deadline.
examples.target_text: Elas estão muito empenhadas em terminar o projeto antes do prazo.

examples.en_text: We are committed to resolving this misunderstanding as quickly as possible.
examples.target_text: Nós estamos empenhados em resolver este mal-entendido o mais rápido possível.

explanation_en: This highly idiomatic connector is used to introduce a fact that proves or illustrates a previous statement, equivalent to 'so much so that' or 'as proof of this.' It is extremely common in spoken Portuguese when building an argument. Learners often struggle with this construction, mistakenly trying to translate 'so much so' literally.

examples.en_text: They loved their trip to Portugal, so much so that they decided to buy a house there.
examples.target_text: Eles adoraram a viagem a Portugal, tanto é que decidiram comprar uma casa lá.

examples.en_text: The boss liked your project very much, so much so that he has already approved it.
examples.target_text: O chefe gostou muito do seu projeto, tanto é que já o aprovou.

examples.en_text: She is very tired today, so much so that she slept all afternoon.
examples.target_text: Ela está muito cansada hoje, tanto é que dormiu durante a tarde toda.

examples.en_text: He really wants to learn Portuguese, so much so that he studies every day.
examples.target_text: Ele quer mesmo aprender português, tanto é que estuda todos os dias.

examples.en_text: We are very close friends, so much so that we travel together every year.
examples.target_text: Nós somos muito amigos, tanto é que viajamos juntos todos os anos.

examples.en_text: That restaurant is excellent, so much so that it is always full of people.
examples.target_text: Aquele restaurante é excelente, tanto é que está sempre cheio de gente.

explanation_en: This colloquial but widely accepted idiom means 'off the top of one's head' or 'from memory' (without checking a source). It is typically paired with verbs like 'saber' (to know) or 'ter' (to have). It is an essential phrase for natural, fluent spoken Portuguese.

examples.en_text: I don't remember his number off the top of my head, I have to check my phone.
examples.target_text: Não me lembro do número dele de cabeça, tenho de ver no telemóvel.

examples.en_text: She can do difficult calculations in her head very quickly.
examples.target_text: Ela consegue fazer contas difíceis de cabeça muito rapidamente.

examples.en_text: I've made this cake so many times that I know the recipe by heart.
examples.target_text: Eu já fiz este bolo tantas vezes que sei a receita de cabeça.

examples.en_text: Off the top of my head, I can't tell you where that street is, but I can look it up on the map.
examples.target_text: De cabeça, não te sei dizer onde fica aquela rua, mas posso pesquisar no mapa.

examples.en_text: I can't say the names of all the countries in Europe off the top of my head.
examples.target_text: Não consigo dizer os nomes de todos os países da Europa de cabeça.

examples.en_text: I'm not sure of the prices off the top of my head, but I think it costs about twenty euros.
examples.target_text: Não tenho a certeza dos preços de cabeça, mas acho que custa cerca de vinte euros.

explanation_en: Equivalent to the English idiom 'a bed of roses,' this phrase describes a situation that is perfect, easy, or without any problems. It is almost always used in the negative ('não é um mar de rosas') or in rhetorical questions to highlight that things are actually quite difficult or chaotic. It is a very common, natural idiom across all registers of Portuguese.

examples.en_text: At the beginning, the new job seemed like a bed of roses, but then the problems appeared.
examples.target_text: No início, o novo trabalho parecia um mar de rosas, mas depois surgiram os problemas.

examples.en_text: No marriage is a bed of roses; all couples have arguments once in a while.
examples.target_text: Nenhum casamento é um mar de rosas; todos os casais têm discussões de vez em quando.

examples.en_text: Living alone in a new country is not a bed of roses, but it helps us grow a lot.
examples.target_text: Viver sozinho num país novo não é um mar de rosas, mas ajuda-nos a crescer bastante.

examples.en_text: Starting your own business is far from being a bed of roses.
examples.target_text: Criar a tua própria empresa está longe de ser um mar de rosas.

examples.en_text: Life with young children is wonderful, but it's not always a bed of roses.
examples.target_text: A vida com filhos pequenos é maravilhosa, mas nem sempre é um mar de rosas.

examples.en_text: He thought university life would be a bed of roses, but now he spends his nights studying.
examples.target_text: Ele achava que a vida universitária seria um mar de rosas, mas agora passa as noites a estudar.

explanation_en: A highly colloquial, idiomatic filler phrase used to say 'let's be honest,' 'let's face it,' or 'let's agree.' It is used to prompt the listener to agree with an obvious or highly likely truth. It is very common in informal conversations, podcasts, and opinion columns.

examples.en_text: Let's face it, my mother's food is the best in the world.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que a comida da minha mãe é a melhor do mundo.

examples.en_text: Rio de Janeiro is beautiful, but, let's be honest, the heat in the summer is almost unbearable.
examples.target_text: O Rio de Janeiro é lindo, mas, vamos combinar, o calor no verão é quase insuportável.

examples.en_text: Technology helps a lot, but let's face it, sometimes it causes more trouble than it helps.
examples.target_text: A tecnologia ajuda muito, mas vamos combinar que às vezes ela mais atrapalha do que ajuda.

examples.en_text: Learning Portuguese is wonderful, but let's be honest, the pronunciation can be quite difficult at the beginning.
examples.target_text: Aprender português é maravilhoso, mas vamos combinar que a pronúncia pode ser bem difícil no começo.

examples.en_text: His new car is amazing, but let's face it, the price was absurd.
examples.target_text: O carro novo dele é incrível, mas vamos combinar que o preço foi um absurdo.

examples.en_text: He said he was going to call, but let's be honest, he always forgets these things.
examples.target_text: Ele disse que ia ligar, mas vamos combinar que ele sempre esquece essas coisas.

explanation_en: This colorful idiom literally translates to 'to throw everything into the fan,' equivalent to the English 'the shit hits the fan' or 'to expose all the dirty laundry.' It is used when someone decides to reveal scandalous secrets or expose corruption publicly. It carries a highly informal, dramatic tone.

examples.en_text: If they don't pay me what they owe, I'm going to blow the whistle on everything.
examples.target_text: Se eles não me pagarem o que devem, eu vou jogar tudo no ventilador.

examples.en_text: After the fight, she decided to expose everything and tell his secrets to the family.
examples.target_text: Depois da briga, ela decidiu jogar tudo no ventilador e contar os segredos dele para a família.

examples.en_text: The former company director threatened to blow the whistle on everything if he were fired.
examples.target_text: O ex-diretor da empresa ameaçou jogar tudo no ventilador se fosse demitido.

examples.en_text: I didn't want to cause trouble, but he annoyed me so much that I ended up spilling all the beans.
examples.target_text: Eu não queria criar confusão, mas ele me irritou tanto que acabei jogando tudo no ventilador.

examples.en_text: Before his partner blew the whistle on everything, he preferred to confess the mistake.
examples.target_text: Antes que o sócio jogasse tudo no ventilador, ele preferiu confessar o erro.

examples.en_text: If you don't tell me the truth, I'm going to expose everything at the next building meeting.
examples.target_text: Se você não me disser a verdade, eu vou jogar tudo no ventilador na próxima reunião de condomínio.

explanation_en: This idiomatic phrase means 'who knows,' 'heaven knows,' or 'god knows.' It is used to express complete uncertainty or skepticism about how or why something happened. It is highly common in everyday spoken Portuguese and informal writing.

examples.en_text: He left the keys somewhere and now who knows where they are.
examples.target_text: Ele deixou as chaves em algum lado e agora sabe-se lá onde estão.

examples.en_text: They decided to cancel the trip at the last minute, heaven knows why.
examples.target_text: Eles decidiram cancelar a viagem à última hora, sabe-se lá porquê.

examples.en_text: If you don't study for the exam, who knows what will happen.
examples.target_text: Se não estudares para o exame, sabe-se lá o que vai acontecer.

examples.en_text: That classic car must have cost heaven knows how much money.
examples.target_text: Aquele carro clássico deve ter custado sabe-se lá quanto dinheiro.

examples.en_text: She went for a walk and who knows when she will return.
examples.target_text: Ela foi dar uma volta e sabe-se lá quando é que regressa.

examples.en_text: He is very quiet today, goodness knows what is going through his mind.
examples.target_text: Ele está muito calado hoje, sabe-se lá o que lhe passa pela cabeça.

explanation_en: This phrase means 'it gives me the impression' or 'I get the feeling.' It is a natural way to express a subjective feeling or observation without stating it as an absolute fact. It is a key conversational tool for advanced learners to soften their opinions.

examples.en_text: This new rule gives me the impression that they want to complicate things.
examples.target_text: Essa nova regra me dá a impressão de que eles querem complicar as coisas.

examples.en_text: He gave me the impression that he was very tired during the meeting.
examples.target_text: Ele me deu a impressão de que estava muito cansado durante a reunião.

examples.en_text: It doesn't give me the impression that it's going to rain today; the sky is very clear.
examples.target_text: Não me dá a impressão de que vai chover hoje, o céu está bem limpo.

examples.en_text: His behavior gives me the impression that he doesn't want to stay at the company.
examples.target_text: O comportamento dele me dá a impressão de que ele não quer continuar na empresa.

examples.en_text: This old city always gives me the impression that time has stopped.
examples.target_text: Essa cidade antiga sempre me dá a impressão de que o tempo parou.

examples.en_text: Their silence gives me the impression that something is wrong.
examples.target_text: O silêncio deles me dá a impressão de que algo está errado.
